⚠️ Prepare for potential flash flooding, landslides, and travel delays this weekend over the North Central Coast Region of Vietnam and Central Laos due to an incoming tropical cyclone⚠️

Invest area 93W has successfully upgraded to a tropical depression, named 20W internationally, but named Jacinto in the Philippines. 
The system currently has modest sustained winds of 56km/h, with gusts of 74, and some intensification is expected over the next 24 hours as the system moves gradually curves towards the southwest, heading for Vietnam. 
Peak intensity guidance suggest this system intensifying to 65 to 85km/h in this timeframe - tropical storm status. 
As the system approaches the Vietnam coast Friday night, intense downpours are expected to develop across the region. 

By early Saturday evening, the tropical storm will make landfall between Dong Ha and Vinh, traveling southwestward inland, bringing potentially life-threatening flash flooding into central Laos and eastern Thailand. 

The threat of torrential downpours will end by midday Sunday as the system weakens and travels further inland. 

Forecasted worst hit locations: 
Vietnam; From Dong Hoi all the way north to Hainan and all areas in between. 

Laos; All of central Laos, from Salavan to Muang Kham.

Thailand; Eastern portion of the country, highest rainfall amounts near Laos borders. 

Hazards: 
• Rainfall rates locally reach 1 to 1.5 inches per hour
• Rainfall totals ranging 3 to 6 inches, with localized amounts of 10+ inches over inland sections of Vietnams North Central Coast, and central Laos. 
• Potential for landslides and dangerous flash flooding 

Currently winds may gust to 50 to 70km/h over the shores of Vietnam as the system makes landfall, but no major wind concerns exist. 

Stay tuned for more updates! #Jacinto #Tropicalstorm #Tropicaldepression #Flooding #Vietnam
